about.title: Livingston Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath is often slow and confusing. In a small community like Livingston, many of the properties where people get hurt—grocery stores, apartment complexes, medical offices, and small retail spots near Main Street and F Street—are owned by local businesses or landlords who carry insurance meant to handle exactly this kind of claim. Under California law, proving fault usually means showing the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazard like a wet floor, broken step, or uneven walkway and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why what happens right after a fall matters: photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage can make a real difference later. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these claims and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Livingston Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network can help identify and gather the kind of evidence that supports this element.

items.title: Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage at Livingston stores and businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're told you were partly at fault for a fall, California's pure comparative fault rule generally allows recovery reduced by your share of responsibility, not eliminated entirely.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Livingston?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city or county building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth talking to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the store or landlord says I wasn't watching where I was going?
items.answer: That's a common response from property owners and their insurers, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. California's comparative fault rule means your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault, not wiped out completely. An attorney can help evaluate the specific facts of your fall.

items.question: Is Livingston too small for a business to have surveillance video?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Many stores and apartment complexes along corridors like Hammatt Avenue and Walnut Avenue use security cameras, even in a smaller community like Livingston. If you fell somewhere with cameras, requesting preservation of that footage quickly is one of the most useful things you can do.
